quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Provide you with an escape route.
Welcome other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Welcome other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see and be seen, avoid hazards, escape from danger, and keep you out of other vehicles' blind spots. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. Use your left foot to operate it. Lift the lever to shift up to a higher gear. Press it down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Always slow down.
Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
Accelerate drastically.
Not worry about your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to stabilize your suspension. Keep your speed steady or speed up gradually as you turn.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Too dangerous to be used by inexperienced operators.
Best when used by itself.
Meant to occasionally assist the rear brake.
To be used with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: To be used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where is the engine cut-off switch usually located?

options.text: Near the left handgrip
Near the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The engine cut-off switch is near the right handgrip. Know the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking alcohol, it is a good idea to do any of the following, except:

options.text: Arrange for a safe ride home for your friend.
Occupy your friend with activities to distract them from drinking.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Stop a friend from riding while impaired. Arrange another ride home, involve them in other activities to slow their drinking, keep them from leaving before they are sober, and ask other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: The control for the rear brake is usually located:

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake is usually operated with your right foot.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: In the front of the group.
Right behind the leader.
At the back of the group.
Wherever they are most comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This lets experienced riders watch them from the back.

questions.question: Can cold tablets and other common drugs affect your ability to ride a motorcycle safely?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
No, they usually won't affect your ability to ride safely.
No, they pose no risk to your riding ability.
No, over-the-counter drugs are always safe to take before riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn about the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: When riding at night compared to riding during the day, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride more slowly.
Leave more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.
Tailgate other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgate other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase the space between you and other vehicles. Use other vehicles' headlights to help you see ahead. Adjust your lane position as needed, especially at night. Never tailgate.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for emergencies.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for emergencies.
Squeeze only the front brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. This habit will help you stop quickly in emergencies. Practice using both brakes together.

questions.question: When turning your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handlebar grip in the opposite direction you want to turn.
Don't hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Don't lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handlebar grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When moving faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn causes the motorcycle to lean the right way.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars are above your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch the ground with your feet while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to reach and use all controls easily.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire has gone flat while riding?

options.text: You hear a hissing noise from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.
You cannot accelerate.
The rear brake stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. Riders rarely hear a tire fail while riding.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the driver will properly yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee the driver will properly yield to you.
It means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will give you the right-of-way. Don't rely on it as a guarantee.

questions.question: How is passing on a motorcycle different from passing in a car?

options.text: Visibility is more critical for a motorcycle.
Visibility is less important for a motorcycle.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the roadway.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is more critical for a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: The basic passing techniques are the same as in a car. However, visibility is more important for motorcycles. Motorcycles are smaller and easier to miss. They can easily disappear into a driver's blind spot.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if possible.
Stay seated and lift your feet off the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight. Just before hitting the obstacle, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: Why is riding directly beside another vehicle discouraged?

options.text: You may have trouble getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in their blind spot. The driver may change lanes without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Any time you slow down or stop
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you slow down or stop
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover your ankles
Hearing protection
Pants made of soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or strong material, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection.

questions.question: What happens when you ride next to another vehicle?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because you have limited escape routes.
You should only do this during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another vehicle. The driver may not see you in their blind spot and could move into your lane. Riding alongside a vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All of it

questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What does a properly-fitted motorcycle allow?

options.text: Your feet can touch the ground while you sit on the seat.
The seat is level with your waist.
The seat is 10 inches above your waist.
The seat is 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet can touch the ground while you sit on the seat.
questions.explanation: A properly-fitted motorcycle lets you touch the ground with your feet when sitting on the seat. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
